steps.title: Establish the main colour
steps.action: Build an even coat of Caliban Green over the green armour.
steps.detail: Use a brush large enough to cover each accessible surface without scrubbing. Thin the paint on the palette until it flows from the tip without leaving a ridge; test there first and remove any hanging drop. Let a coat dry before adding another. Green needs room to stay dark. Do not turn whole panels into the highlight colour.
steps.lookFor: The primer no longer shows through, while the smallest sculpted lines remain open.
steps.simpleExplanation: Begin with a smooth foundation on the green armour. Do not try to cover it in one heavy pass.

steps.title: Separate the materials
steps.action: Use Mephiston Red for red cloth or weapon panels. Use Rakarth Flesh for parchment and bone details. Use Leadbelcher for exposed weapon metal. Use Abaddon Black for weapon casings and flexible joints.
steps.detail: Follow raised folds on cloth; follow edges on hard panels. Keep the darkest colour close to the attachment point and between teeth or folds. Keep the casing separate from the barrel and magazine fittings. Keep highlights narrow so these areas remain visually black. Work from the deepest accessible area out toward raised parts. Let adjacent colours dry before repairing a boundary.
steps.lookFor: The main colour stays clearly separated from the other painted areas, even before highlights.
steps.simpleExplanation: Place the other colours neatly before adding shade. Precise boundaries do more than extra detail at this stage.

steps.title: Place the darks
steps.action: Add controlled shadows to the specific areas below, keeping raised surfaces clear.
steps.detail: Guide Nuln Oil into the recessed parts of the green armour. Use Carroburg Crimson in the recesses of red cloth or weapon panels. Use Seraphim Sepia in the recesses of parchment and bone details. Use Nuln Oil in the recesses of exposed weapon metal. Load a small amount, touch the intended recess and guide it along a short section. Use a clean, barely damp brush to lift pooling while it is still wet. Work one region at a time and leave it alone once drying begins. A broad stain can be repaired with the relevant base colour after it dries.
steps.lookFor: The recesses are darker, with no large glossy pools left on the raised surfaces.
steps.simpleExplanation: Put shadow where surfaces meet or fold inward. It is easier to deepen a small shadow later than to undo a flood.

steps.title: Recover the main surface
steps.action: Restore Caliban Green on the open faces of the green armour, leaving the recesses dark.
steps.detail: Keep a small gap from each shaded seam. Where the recovery colour is lighter than the foundation, build the transition in thin passes and leave a little of the darker base visible near the recess. If the colour is the same as the base, this is a clean-up pass, not an extra highlight.
steps.lookFor: The main colour looks clear again and the shaded lines remain crisp.
steps.simpleExplanation: Bring back the main colour on the raised areas without erasing the shadows.

steps.title: Choose where the light lands
steps.action: Pick out the brow, shoulder rims and forward knees with Warpstone Glow, then add smaller accents of Moot Green.
steps.detail: Where an edge protrudes, use the side of a pointed brush with very light pressure. For a line on a flat surface, brace both hands and paint a short section at a time with the tip. The final colour belongs only on selected corners and upper edges, not around every panel.
steps.lookFor: The brightest marks gather around the upper part of the miniature; the main colour still occupies most of each surface.
steps.simpleExplanation: Add a little light, then an even smaller amount of the brightest colour. Keep the shadows visible.

steps.title: Bring the details into focus
steps.action: Refine the other materials one at a time, following the paint map below.
steps.detail: Restore Mephiston Red where needed, then use Evil Sunz Scarlet on the raised parts of red cloth or weapon panels. Restore Rakarth Flesh where needed, then use Ushabti Bone on the raised parts of parchment and bone details. Restore Leadbelcher where needed, then use Ironbreaker on the raised parts of exposed weapon metal. Restore Abaddon Black where needed, then use Eshin Grey on the raised parts of weapon casings and flexible joints. Keep every highlight smaller than its foundation and preserve shaded seams. Turn the miniature toward the brush for control.
steps.lookFor: Secondary colours remain clear without overpowering the face and upper body.
steps.simpleExplanation: Brighten the details selectively. Preserve dark gaps between neighbouring materials.

steps.title: Finish the focal point
steps.action: Use Mephiston Red and then Evil Sunz Scarlet for eye lenses.
steps.detail: Place the brighter red along the lower front of each lens; keep a dark border. Brace your painting hand against the handle hand and test the brush tip on the palette first. If a mark spreads too far, let it dry and repair its border before trying again.
steps.lookFor: The small accent is contained, balanced and readable at normal viewing distance.
steps.simpleExplanation: Make this the smallest, most deliberate mark in the study. A clean accent is better than an oversized one.

steps.title: Ground it and take a final look
steps.action: Apply Stirland Mud to the base, allow it to dry fully, then paint the rim with Abaddon Black.
steps.detail: Use an old brush or texture tool to keep the texture away from the feet and finished paint. Follow the product guidance for application and drying. Once dry, check the miniature under a broad neutral light and from the distance you would normally hold it. Repair any accidental colour crossings with the relevant base paint. Transfers, freehand banners and optional varnish are separate finishing choices; follow their product instructions if you add them.
steps.lookFor: A tidy base rim, intact shadows and a clear focal point. Nothing is marked finished automatically; decide whether the result meets your own goal.
steps.simpleExplanation: Finish the base, inspect the boundaries and stop when the miniature reads clearly. More paint is not always an improvement.

steps.title: Establish the main colour
steps.action: Build an even coat of Runelord Brass over the brass body plates.
steps.detail: Use a brush large enough to cover each accessible surface without scrubbing. Thin the paint on the palette until it flows from the tip without leaving a ridge; test there first and remove any hanging drop. Let a coat dry before adding another. A metallic highlight needs very little paint. Let the existing brass show through instead of coating every surface in silver. steps.action: Use Leadbelcher for exposed joints and weapon mechanisms. Use Abaddon Black for the weapon casing.
steps.detail: Keep joint cavities dark and catch only the exposed ridges. A restrained casing makes the energy coils appear brighter. Work from the deepest accessible area out toward raised parts. Let adjacent colours dry before repairing a boundary.

steps.simpleExplanation: Place the other colours neatly before adding shade. Precise boundaries do more than extra detail at this stage.

steps.title: Place the darks
steps.action: Add controlled shadows to the specific areas below, keeping raised surfaces clear.

Load a small amount, touch the intended recess and guide it along a short section. Use a clean, barely damp brush to lift pooling while it is still wet. Work one region at a time and leave it alone once drying begins. A broad stain can be repaired with the relevant base colour after it dries.
steps.lookFor: The recesses are darker, with no large glossy pools left on the raised surfaces.
steps.simpleExplanation: Put shadow where surfaces meet or fold inward. It is easier to deepen a small shadow later than to undo a flood.

steps.title: Recover the main surface

steps.simpleExplanation: Bring back the main colour on the raised areas without erasing the shadows.
